title: Peering into a star factory
caption: Part of the star-forming region Messier 17, imaged by ESO's 3.6-meter telescope
celestial: Horseshoe Nebula, Lobster Nebula, M 17, Messier 17, Omega Nebula, Swan Nebula · constellation Sagittarius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Red stars, bluer stars, a diffuse glow and dark patches fill this color-coded infrared view of the south-western part of Messier 17, a star-forming region in our galaxy.

Each color tells you something. Red objects are young stars heavily hidden by dust. Bluer ones are either stars in the foreground or well-developed massive stars whose intense light ionizes the hydrogen around them. The diffuse glow almost everywhere comes from hydrogen atoms forming again as protons and electrons recombine. The dark areas are where thick dust blocks the light of objects behind it, and that same dust makes many stars look redder.

In the upper left sits a cluster of young stars so deeply buried in the nebula that it cannot be seen in optical light, yet it shows up clearly in infrared. The images were taken with the SOFI camera on ESO's 3.6-meter telescope.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.91 x 4.81 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.9 × 7.7 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared composite from SOFI uses J, H and Ks filters, rendered as blue, green and red respectively.
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, and the buried star cluster in the upper left cannot be seen at all in visible light.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Exposures of five minutes each were made through J, H and Ks filters, with another 15 minutes on separate sky frames. The field covers about 5 by 5 arcminutes, roughly 3% of the full Moon, with north up. Objects in the far upper left corner look slightly stretched because of an optical effect at the edge of the field.
alt: An infrared field of red and blue stars with diffuse glowing gas and dark dusty patches, and a cluster of young stars in the upper left.
